steps.action: Call your bank's anti-scam hotline now. Say you were tricked into sending a transfer. Ask them to stop it, and to freeze your accounts if the scammer may still get in.
steps.contact: your bank's anti-scam hotline (DBS/POSB 1800 339 6963, OCBC 6363 3333, UOB 6255 0160)

steps.action: File a police report online, or at your nearest Neighbourhood Police Centre. For urgent help, call 999.
If your bank will not help, make a complaint to the bank. If you are not happy with its final reply, file a claim with FIDReC. It must be within 6 months of the bank's final reply.
steps.organisation: the Financial Industry Disputes Resolution Centre (FIDReC)

evidence.quote: You may file a police report online or in person
The consumer must file the claim within 6 months of receiving a final reply
there is a limit of S$150,000 per claim for adjudication of disputes
the Shared Responsibility Framework for phishing scams

extra.notes: No reimbursement rule covers a transfer the victim made. The MAS/IMDA Shared Responsibility Framework (from 16 December 2024) covers phishing scams only, so it is not listed as the law. capAmount null: S$150,000 is FIDReC's adjudication limit, not a refund cap. The Police Hotline 1800-255-0000 takes scam information; the report itself is filed online or at a police centre. ScamShield says a bank's Kill Switch can freeze all accounts. FIDReC's 6-month window is in the action text with deadlineDays null.
